text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: page fired PD-987654 — inference-proxy.latency.p95 > 300ms in eu-west-1 (auto-escalation rules matched)
oncall-mike: acked — I'm on it. pulling up dashboards
sre-jen: thanks. I'm checking recent deploys, nothing in CI for proxy in last 2h.
carla: alert looks like a short burst from synthetic canary, any customer reports?
oncall-mike: no customer tickets in zendesk, no error spikes in logs. latency graphs: https://grafana.redwood/inference/proxy?from=-10m show a 90s blip peaking ~420ms then trending back down.
sre-alex: I'm seeing simultaneous small uptick in egress network errors from a subset of backend hosts (3/24), maybe transient host-level NIC flapping.
sre-jen: can you paste the host IDs?
sre-alex: host-az1-07, host-az1-11, host-az2-02
oncall-mike: running quick health checks: ```for h in host-az1-07 host-az1-11 host-az2-02; do ssh $h 'sudo ethtool -S eth0 | grep rx_errors || true'; done``` nothing obvious in rx_errors, but dmesg on host-az1-11 shows a couple of mlx5 resets ~2m ago.
carla: incident-bot shows PD auto-suppression rule applied previously for the same metric — are we in a suppression window?
sre-jen: good question. PD config shows a 3-min suppression window for repeated p95 spikes on inference-proxy in eu-west-1 (to reduce flapping). This was a new synthetic canary run.
oncall-mike: pagerduty-bot: did PD auto-resolve yet?
pagerduty-bot: PD update: alert acknowledged by oncall-mike. No automatic resolution triggered yet.
sre-alex: I can repro a small spike by replaying a short heavy multi-tenant batch on the affected hosts; suggests momentary kernel driver hiccup under burst.
carla: since no customer impact and only 90s blip, I vote to let suppression do its thing; mark as monitored.
sre-jen: agree. I'll keep tailing logs and set a short watch. If it comes back within 5m we'll do a brief remediation (drain host-az1-11).
oncall-mike: creating a quick note in the thread for oncall handoff: if it reoccurs >3x in 15m escalate to infra and run a rolling drain.
sre-alex: can we add a temporary routing fallback to another region if eu-west keeps bouncing? not yet, that would be heavier.
carla: customer impact check: ran a query against prod request logs for last 10m, error rate zero, median latency normal. copy of query: ```SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE region='eu-west-1' AND status >= 500 AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'``` returned 0.
pagerduty-bot: PD note: incident still open, suppressed alerts count=1.
sre-jen: oncall-mike — i'll take an initial 10m watch, then hand to alex at +10 if stable.
oncall-mike: sounds good. handoff ETA 10m. I'm going to set a short dashboard alert: 
```
alert: short-eu-p95
metric: inference-proxy.latency.p95{region="eu-west-1"}
threshold: 300ms
window: 1m
notify: eng-sre (pagerduty suppressed)
```
sre-alex: noted. setting an infra watch on host-az1-11 and adding a quick syslog capture to S3: `sudo journalctl -u systemd -o short-iso > /tmp/syslog-snap && aws s3 cp /tmp/syslog-snap s3://redwood-diagnostics/1745552468-host-az1-11.log`
incident-bot: PD update: alert resolved automatically (auto-resolve by policy)
sre-jen: saw auto-resolve at ~1745552520. spike cleared.
oncall-mike: thanks. wrapping up: - no customer impact - likely transient NIC/driver hiccup on a couple hosts - suppression prevented noisy paging - we set short watch and documented a handoff plan if it repeats
sre-alex: I'll follow up with infra to keep an eye on firmware/drivers on those hosts, and schedule a non-urgent host reboot window if we see reoccurrence.
carla: filing a quick post-note: "PD-987654: transient p95 spike eu-west-1, auto-resolved, no customer impact, potential NIC driver reset on host-az1-11. follow-up: infra to track firmware/drivers."
sre-jen: tagging oncall rotation: next oncall is @sre-alex — please pick this up at +10 if still lingering. :white_check_mark:
oncall-mike: handing off to alex in 10. thanks team :thumbsup:
carla: adding retrospective note to runbook about lowering sensitivity of the synthetic canary (it generated a suppression/handshake).
pagerduty-bot: PD note: incident closed at 1745552542
sre-alex: acknowledging handoff. I'll take the follow-up and file an infra ticket.
carla: closing thread, will log in incident tracker with the notes above. :lock:
